content.text:
The campaign is finished and submitted. The best composition I measured is **index 45 (Bi 0.10, Cu 0.49, V 0.41)**, with a photocurrent of 11.5 µA.

The budget allowed only 3 photocurrent measurements across 143 compositions, and all 3 are used, so this is the best of three points rather than a search of the library. I don't know how it compares with the library's true best.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 45 | 0.10 / 0.49 / 0.41 | **11.5 µA** |
| 4 | 0.40 / 0.19 / 0.41 | 8.3 µA |
| 44 | 0.09 / 0.52 / 0.39 | 3.2 µA |

- **First two picks:** I measured one composition from each of two regions I expected to work. Index 4 is a bismuth vanadate–like composition with some Cu; index 45 is in the copper vanadate region.
- **Third pick:** I spent 3 of the 5 XRD scans on 45 and two neighbours. All three share mostly the same crystal phases. Index 44 has more of a Cu-rich phase, and index 103 has an extra phase that 45 and 44 don't.
- **What that suggests:** 44 has a bit more Cu and less V than 45, and its photocurrent fell sharply. So the best area is probably at 45 or on its higher-V side.
- **Main remaining candidate:** Index 103 (Bi 0.13, Cu 0.42, V 0.45) sits on that higher-V side and was never measured, so it could beat 45.
